title: Installments Held at the Pre-Default Amount on a Manually Paid Plan
content:
Desk guidance for **Patient Payment Plans**: on a plan paid manually, installments next in line keep the pre-default installment when a defaulted plan is put back in force.

## The rule

On a plan without automatic payments on whose ledger a payment by check has been posted, the next two installments stay at the pre-default installment; on a plan without automatic payments and no payment by check, the next installment stays at it; on any other plan none is held. The held installments are taken out of the reinstated balance at the pre-default installment and out of the installments counted, and the reinstated installment applies from the installment after them.

| Automatic payments on the plan | Payment by check on the plan ledger | Installments held at the pre-default installment |
|---|---|---|
| No | Yes, at least one | 2 |
| No | None | 1 |
| Yes | any | 0 |

A *payment by check* is any payment on the plan ledger, of any kind, whose method is a check. The *pre-default installment* is the regular monthly installment the plan carried when it defaulted.

## Hypothetical figures

Reinstated balance 630.00; pre-default installment 90.00; the balance is spread over 7 installments.

| Held | Working | Reinstated installment, from the installment after those held |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 630.00 divided by 7 | 90.00 |
| 1 | 630.00 less 90.00, that is 540.00, divided by 6 | 90.00 |
| 2 | 630.00 less 180.00, that is 450.00, divided by 5 | 90.00 |

With a reinstated balance of 700.00 instead: none held gives 100.00; one held gives 610.00 divided by 6, that is 101.67; two held give 520.00 divided by 5, that is 104.00. The quotient is taken to the nearest cent, an exact half cent being rounded up.
